youtube_description:
Ever feel like you can't trust anything anyone says anymore? David felt that way: "Save, O LORD, for the faithful have vanished" (Psalm 12:1).

The flatterers speak "with a double heart" (Psalm 12:2). In Hebrew, be-lev va-lev (beh-LEV vah-LEV): with a heart and a heart. One heart for show, another underneath. Against all that noise, God's words are pure, like silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times (Psalm 12:6).

Today's step: guard your own words. Mean what you say, and fill your mind with words you can trust.

Day 12 of the Psalms, one chapter a day. Follow @thebibleexplainedai so you don't miss Psalm 13.

Read it: Psalm 12:1-8
